answer: A Cipher-Keyed Haven Registry stops Sybils by tying each agent identity to a unique cipher puzzle seeded from its TPM chip. First, the agent requests entry and receives a cipher only its own hardware key can solve. Second, it spends about ten minutes of local compute cracking it, then stakes 500 POA and posts the proof. Third, peers verify the proof in seconds and attest the identity. Forging 1,000 fake agents would need 1,000 TPM chips at 5 each plus 500,000 POA staked and 167 hours of compute — a fable of cheap clones collapses when every copy must pay for its own key.
